answer:
INTRODUCTION
The primary failure mode is wax gel formation during the 3-day shutdown, causing the 8-inch flowline to plug and requiring restart pressures that exceed the Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure (MAOP). The intervention modifies the operational protocol by maintaining a high-shear flow profile at a specific velocity and temperature to disrupt gel kinetics. This approach is grounded in the principle that thermal gradients drive wax precipitation. By maintaining flow, the thermal boundary layer is minimized, keeping the bulk fluid above the gelation temperature and preventing wax from reaching the wall. This avoids the need for chemical inhibitors, which are not available on the subsea system.

PARAMETERS
PARAMETER: Flow velocity — 2.5 m/s — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Operating temperature — 55 C — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Gelation temperature — 45 C — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Internal diameter — 0.20 m — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Restart pressure limit — 100% of MAOP — ASSUMPTION

EXPECTED EFFECT
Increasing flow velocity to 2.5 m/s reduces the thermal boundary layer thickness, maintaining the oil at the wall above the 45 C gelation threshold. This prevents the formation of a solid wax-gel deposit that would otherwise increase restart pressure. The high-shear profile also disrupts any nascent wax agglomerates, ensuring the restart pressure remains under the MAOP constraint. This hydraulic management strategy is effective for waxy crude systems where chemical injection is not viable.

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE
This proposal respects the constraint that no chemical injection skid exists by relying purely on hydraulic and thermal management. It ensures restart pressure remains under the MAOP by preventing the pressure spike associated with wax plugging. The device of record remains the 8-inch subsea multiphase flowline; no hardware modifications are proposed, only a change in operational protocol.

FALSIFICATION TEST
TEST TEMPERATURE: 55 C ambient. DURATION: 3 days (simulating shutdown). SAMPLE SIZE n: 3 flowline segments. PASS/FAIL CRITERIA: Fail if wax-gel thickness exceeds 2 mm at the wall or if restart pressure exceeds 85% of MAOP. Pass if fluid remains mobile and restart pressure is below 80% of MAOP.
